Priya (customer): Hey team — after the networking change this morning our Private deployment started failing to fetch keys from the KMS/HSM. Errors in the app: "kms: failed to fetch key: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = "transport: authentication handshake failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority""
Alice (support): Thanks Priya — can you paste the exact log lines and the KMS hostname you hit? also which subnet/bastion you can run tests from?
Priya (customer): logs: `2026-05-11T09:12:03Z error kms: fetch key id=proj/payments err="x509: certificate signed by unknown authority"` Host: `kms-priv.prod.internal:443`. We have a bastion in the same private subnet (10.40.12.7).
Marco (platform): Quick checklist: DNS resolution, proxy env, firewall egress rules, and any TLS termination devices in-path. Priya can you run `dig +short kms-priv.prod.internal` and `curl -v --connect-timeout 5 https://kms-priv.prod.internal/health` from the bastion?
Priya (customer): dig returns `10.40.8.21`. curl output (truncated):
```
* CONNECT to kms-priv.prod.internal port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 connection established
* server certificate verification failed: certificate has unknown CA.
* Closing connection 0
curl: (51) SSL: certificate verify failed
```
Nate (sre): That lines up with x509 CA issue. Two likely causes: 1) KMS cert changed or intermediate missing, 2) a proxy / TLS terminator replacing cert (corporate TLS-inspect). Can you run `openssl s_client -connect 10.40.8.21:443 -servername kms-priv.prod.internal -showcerts` and paste the cert subject/issuer?
Priya (customer): pasted output: `subject= CN = kms.internal.local` and `issuer= CN = internal-proxy-intermediate`. Chain shows only one cert.
Alice (support): issuer looks like our proxy's intermediate, not the KMS cert. Do you have a transparent TLS proxy on that path? Check the firewall vendor config or any intercepting appliance. Also check `env | grep -i proxy` on host.
Priya (customer): `no_proxy` is set for AWS metadata but not for internal hosts. No HTTP proxy envs on the app container. Firewall team said they rolled a rule to force traffic for certain CIDRs through the new inspection cluster this morning.
Marco (platform): aha. That will break mTLS to the HSM (mutual TLS) — the proxy will not present the client cert to the HSM and will re-sign the server cert, causing client validation to fail. You'll either need an allowlist bypass for KMS/HSM CIDR or an explicit tunnel (CONNECT) that preserves TLS.
Nate (sre): To confirm, capture a quick pcap: `sudo tcpdump -n -s 0 -c 200 host 10.40.8.21 and port 443 -w /tmp/kms.pcap` then check if the server sends a TLS ServerHello or if we see an intermediate MITM. If the proxy terminates, you'll see `Certificate` chain from proxy IP not from HSM IP.
Priya (customer): tcpdump shows server IP 10.40.8.21 but certificate CN is `corp-inspect-proxy.local`. So it's the inspect device.
Alice (support): OK confirmed. Root cause: inspection device performing TLS interception causing x509 errors and breaking mutual auth. Remediation options: 1) add explicit allowlist so traffic to KMS/HSM CIDR bypasses TLS-inspect, 2) configure the proxy as a TCP CONNECT tunnel (no termination) for those destinations, or 3) reconfigure the client to trust the interception CA (not ideal for HSM). Which do you prefer?
Priya (customer): Firewall team prefers allowlist. They asked for exact CIDRs and ports to open. What do you need us to request?
Marco (platform): Open egress to 10.40.8.0/24 (KMS pool) and 10.40.9.0/28 (HSM appliances) on TCP 443 and TCP 15001 (HSM control) from the app subnets. Also ensure SNAT isn't rewriting source cert references — preserve source ports (ephemeral range) and check SNAT port exhaustion.
Nate (sre): Also verify that the customer-managed HSM is expecting mTLS: confirm client cert chain and that the proxy bypass preserves the TCP handshake for client cert exchange. After allowlist, restart a single app pod to test. Repro steps we used: `curl --cacert /etc/ssl/certs/kms-root.pem https://kms-priv.prod.internal/health` should return 200 once bypassed.
infra-bot: Alert: KMS-priv pool 10.40.8.20-30 reported degraded TLS handshakes (5xx) 09:10-09:20 UTC — tied to rule rollout #fw-2026-05-11.
Priya (customer): Firewall team applied the allowlist for the two CIDRs and disabled TLS-inspect for those networks. After that, `curl -v` succeeded and app logs show key fetch OK: `2026-05-11T09:23:12Z info kms: fetched key id=proj/payments`
Alice (support): Great. For follow-up: 1) add automated test in deployment pipeline that verifies mTLS to KMS after network changes (simple curl healthcheck using client cert), 2) document required firewall allowlists and SNAT ephemeral port ranges in the runbook, 3) consider a canary policy for inspection rules that excludes critical control-plane CIDRs.
Priya (customer): Thanks all — rolling this change to remaining regions now. Will follow up if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: note: rolling restart executed for payment-service canary (1 of 3).
